title: Movie Recommendation System
summary: A content based movie recommendation app that helps users discover their next favourite film by analysing movie metadata and finding similar titles using TF-IDF and cosine similarity.
points: How to use the app. Select a movie from the searchable dropdown and click Find Similar Movies. The app returns five recommendations based on the selected film, with movie posters to make browsing easier.

Dataset and data source. Used the TMDB 5000 Movies and TMDB 5000 Credits datasets, commonly available through Kaggle. The movies dataset provides information such as genres, keywords, overview and title, while the credits dataset contains cast and crew details.

Data preprocessing. Loaded both CSV files with Pandas and merged them using the movie title. Parsed the genres, keywords, cast and crew fields from their stored JSON-like format, selected relevant names and combined useful metadata into a single feature for each movie.

Feature engineering. Cleaned the combined text and joined selected movie attributes into a single content description. This helps the system compare movies using information about their content rather than relying on user ratings or viewing history.

TF-IDF vectorization. Used Scikit-learn's TfidfVectorizer to convert the combined movie descriptions into numerical vectors. TF-IDF gives more importance to informative terms and less importance to terms that appear frequently across many movies.
Cosine similarity. Calculated cosine similarity between the movie vectors to measure how closely their content matches. Higher similarity scores indicate movies with more similar metadata.

Recommendation process. Stored the similarity matrix and mapped each movie title to its dataset index. When a user selects a movie, the app retrieves its similarity scores, ranks other movies from highest to lowest and displays the top five recommendations.

Poster integration and deployment. Used the TMDB API to fetch movie posters using movie IDs and displayed the results in a Streamlit interface. Deployed the application online so users can try the recommendation system without running the notebook.

title: SMS Spam Detection
summary: A machine learning project that detects spam messages using natural language processing, TF-IDF and a Linear SVM model. The application helps users identify unwanted messages through a simple web interface.
points: Problem statement. Spam messages often contain fake offers, unwanted advertisements and suspicious links. The goal of this project is to build a machine learning model that can automatically identify whether a message is spam or a normal message called ham.

Dataset preparation. Used a labeled SMS dataset containing messages and their categories. Loaded the data using Pandas and selected the required columns for training. This gave the model examples of both spam and legitimate messages to learn from.

Text preprocessing. Cleaned the messages by converting text to lowercase and removing unwanted characters and links. For example, WIN a FREE prize becomes win a free prize. This helps keep the text consistent before converting it into numerical features.

Train and test split. Divided the dataset into training and testing sets using an 80 to 20 ratio. The training data helps the model learn patterns, while the testing data checks how well it predicts messages it has not seen before.

TF-IDF feature extraction. Used TF-IDF to convert text messages into numerical values that a machine learning model can understand. It gives more importance to useful words and less importance to words that appear frequently across messages. This helps the model identify patterns commonly associated with spam.

Model training. Used a Linear Support Vector Machine, also called Linear SVM, to classify messages as spam or ham. The model learns from the TF-IDF features and finds patterns that help separate the two categories.

Model evaluation. Evaluated the model using accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score. Accuracy measures overall correctness, precision checks how reliable spam predictions are, and recall measures how many actual spam messages are detected. The confusion matrix helps identify incorrect predictions.
Model saving. Saved the trained TF-IDF and Linear SVM pipeline using Pickle. This allows the application to reuse the trained model without repeating the entire training process.

Streamlit application. Built a simple web interface using Streamlit where users can enter a message and check its category. The saved model processes the message and displays whether it is spam or ham.

Results and conclusion. The model achieved 98.39% accuracy on the evaluation dataset, with 99.25% precision, 88.59% recall and a 93.62% F1-score. The project demonstrates how NLP and machine learning can be used to detect spam messages and make predictions through a web application.
